title: Rework tools/guard_rules.py matching structurally (shlex tokens, flag-cluster expansion, case normalization, git global-option stripping)
description:
Follow-up outside the syml-x0m epic, filed 2026-09-24 when /sp:08-harden stalled: five consecutive security reviews each found new regex-blocklist gaps in the Bash guard hook (remediated as syml-x0m.6.3 through 6.10: quoted and split-quoted arguments, quoted program words, command substitution inside -m payloads, git -C/-c and interleaved flags, the short hook-skip flag -n, flag clusters like -Df/-uf/-Rf, glob targets for recursive rm, checkout HEAD . and restore --worktree spellings, core.hooksPath overrides). Per David's decision the harden loop now files guard-hook findings at p3.

This task replaces regex patching with a structural design:
1. Tokenize each simple command with shlex (posix, punctuation_chars) once; fail closed on unbalanced quotes.
2. Normalize tokens: case-fold flags, expand clustered short flags (-Df -> -D -f), strip git global options (-C, -c, --git-dir, --work-tree) before the subcommand, resolve short/long aliases for hook-skip and force flags.
3. Match every rule against the normalized token list, not the raw string.
4. Keep heredoc bodies and commit-message payloads excluded, except when they contain $( or backticks.
5. Port every probe in tests/tools/test_guard_rules.py to the new matcher and add a table-driven test per rule.

Behavior contract: the new ALLOW/BLOCK decisions must be a superset of today's BLOCKs. 100% coverage, ruff, mypy; commit through the normal pre-commit hooks. Blocked on the syml-x0m epic so the harden run's ralph drain (SCOPE=ALL) does not pick it up.

description:

**Spec**: specs/002-syml-language-revision/spec.md §US2 scenarios 9(partial),10,11,12(partial),13; FR-011, FR-013; contracts/03-errors.md

**Files**: src/syml/exceptions.py (ParseError.__str__, filename kw via os.fspath, DuplicateKeyError.message), tests/test_exceptions.py
**Instructions**: `str(ParseError)` MUST read `<filename>:<line>:<column>: <message>` followed by a newline and the offending line text (filename+colon omitted when none known); line/column per §10.2 (1-indexed line, 0-indexed column). `.message`, `.position`, `.line_text`, `.args` layout stay. `DuplicateKeyError.message` becomes `Duplicate key '<key>'`. title: Red: inline key/list-item values mark TextLeafNode.inline True
description:
**Type**: RED (write failing test)
**Story**: US1 — Tree building follows the specification's acceptance rules
**Behavior**: An inline value (text on the same line as its key or list marker, e.g. 'a: Note') must set TextLeafNode.inline=True so its continuation baseline stays open (None) until the first accepted continuation line fixes it (D11), rather than being fixed at the inline text's own column. Concretely: syml.loads('a: Note\n  Big Warning: do not touch') must equal {'a': 'Note\nBig Warning: do not touch'} — 'Big Warning: do not touch' fails the key_value grammar (space before the colon) so it falls through to plain text and should join as continuation prose under 'Note'. Today SymlParser.visit_key_value and visit_value_list_item (src/syml/parsers.py) never set inline=True on the value they attach, so ContainerNode.add_node's 'baseline = None if node.inline else node.level' branch is dead from the parser side, the baseline gets fixed at the inline text's own column (3, for 'Note'), and the continuation line (column 2) fails the baseline check, raising OutOfContextNodeError instead of joining.
**Test file**: tests/test_parsers.py (class TestSimpleParserFunction, via syml.loads — exercise the full parse path)
**Target module**: src/syml/parsers.py (SymlParser.visit_key_value, visit_value_list_item) and src/syml/nodes.py (ContainerNode.add_node already reads node.inline correctly)
**Existing patterns**: tests/test_parsers.py::TestSimpleParserFunction
**Skills**: /pytest-unit-testing
**Instructions**: This leaf is one Test List entry. Write ONE failing test asserting on syml.loads(...) for the example above. Verify it fails on an assertion or the wrong raised exception type, not an import/collection error. Also verify by hand (do not add as a test unless useful) that 'note: hello\n  more: text' still raises OutOfContextNodeError, and that 'key: a\nb' and 'key: a\n    b\n  c' and '-   name: Alice\n  role: admin' still raise OutOfContextNodeError once inline is honored — these are separate already-passing acceptance scenarios (specs/acceptance-specs/US01-tree-building-acceptance.feature) that must not regress.
**Done when**: tests/test_parsers.py fails with an AssertionError or wrong-exception-type failure (not a collection error) via uv run pytest tests/test_parsers.py --no-cov.
**Commit**: Stage the failing test, then run .venv/bin/python -m tools.commit_red <task-id>. Do NOT push.

title: Red: §4.1 ws excludes tab as separator
description:
Type: TDD_RED
Story: US3 — Lines lex per the §4.1 grammar as printed
Spec: SYML-SPECIFICATION.md §4.1 grammar `ws = ~" +"` (comment: "Required whitespace (spaces only; a tab does not satisfy this, see §7.5)"); §7.5 reiterates the tab-is-not-separator-whitespace rule.
Bug found by: syml-x0m.5.4.20 (Verify acceptance test passes for US3) while binding tests/acceptance/test_us03_line_lexing.py. `src/syml/parsers.py` line 56 currently has `ws = ~"[ \t]+"` (tab accepted), which contradicts the spec. Concretely:
  - `syml.loads("key:\tv")` (tab immediately after colon, no space) currently returns `{"key": "v"}` — it should return the scalar string `"key:\tv"` unchanged, since a tab never satisfies the `ws` separator and there is no key_value guard without a space.
  - `syml.loads("key: \tv")` (space then tab) currently returns `{"key": "v"}` (tab silently dropped) — it should return `{"key": "\tv"}`, since after the one required separator space, the tab is ordinary value content.
Failing acceptance scenarios (once bound, still red until this is fixed): "A tab immediately after the colon is never separator whitespace" and "A tab after the separating space is preserved as value content" in specs/acceptance-specs/US03-line-lexing.feature.
Write ONE failing unit test in tests/test_parsers.py (or wherever `ws` grammar behavior is already tested) asserting `syml.loads("key:\tv") == "key:\tv"` (or equivalent grammar-level assertion) — it must fail on the assertion, not on a collection/import error. Do not fix the grammar in this task.
close_reason: Added failing unit test proving tab is incorrectly accepted as ws separator (§4.1)

title: Red: comment-only line leaks VisitationError
description: Discovered while binding tests/acceptance/test_us05_error_taxonomy.py's acceptance test for FR-009 (no third-party exception may escape loads). `syml.loads('####')` (a comment line that is entirely '#'/'//' markers, e.g. '####', with no text after them) currently raises `parsimonious.exceptions.VisitationError` instead of succeeding or raising a `syml.ParseError` subclass. Root cause: in src/syml/parsers.py's `visit_comment` (around line 132-135), the grammar rule `comment = ~"(#|//+)+" text?" makes the trailing `text?` optional; when it does not match, Parsimonious visits it to `None` (not a zero-length node), so `text.pnode` raises AttributeError, which Parsimonious re-wraps as VisitationError. Repro: `python -c \"import syml; syml.loads('####')\"` raises parsimonious.exceptions.VisitationError: AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'pnode'. Write ONE failing unit test in tests/test_parsers.py (e.g. in a class near TestVisitQuotedValueDecoderDefectConversion) asserting that parsing a comment-only document such as '####' either returns a plain string result or raises a syml.exceptions.ParseError subclass -- NOT a parsimonious exception. The test must fail on the assertion (AttributeError from visit_comment / VisitationError), not on an import error. Follow the RED protocol: stage only the failing test, then commit via .venv/bin/python -m tools.commit_red <task-id>; do not push.

Verify with: uv run pytest tests/test_parsers.py --no-cov and uv run pytest --no-cov (full suite green), plus manually: python -c "import syml; print(syml.loads('####'))" no longer raises a non-ParseError exception.

title: Red: grammar quoted_value recognizes double-quoted values
description:
**Type**: RED (write failing test)
**Story**: US6 — Quoted strings work exactly where §4.7 says they do
**Behavior**: The parser grammar's `quoted_value` rule only defines `single_quoted` (src/syml/parsers.py, `quoted_value = single_quoted`) — there is no `double_quoted` grammar production at all, despite `quoting.decode_double_quoted` existing and being unit-tested in isolation (tests/test_quoting.py). title: Red: bare-line value position does not recognize quoting (D2)
description:
**Type**: RED (write failing test)
**Story**: US6 — Quoted strings work exactly where §4.7 says they do
**Behavior**: A bare line (a standalone root scalar, or a continuation line — anything that reaches the grammar's `line` rule's bare `value` alternative, not the dedicated inline positions after `key:` or `- `) is NEVER quote-decoded; a leading `'` or `"` there is ordinary text.

**Discovered from**: syml-x0m.5.7.20 (Verify acceptance test passes for US6). `just acceptance` scenario "A continuation line does not quote-decode" fails:
  Given a SYML document "key: He said\n  'yes'"
  Then the result equals {'key': "He said\n'yes'"}
Actual: `syml.loads("key: He said\n  'yes'")` returns `{'key': 'He said\nyes'}` — the continuation line `  'yes'` is being quote-decoded (single-quoted decode strips the quotes) when it should stay literal text.

Root cause is broader than just continuations: a terminated quote on a bare ROOT-SCALAR line also wrongly decodes today —
  `syml.loads("'yes'")` returns `'yes'` (decoded) instead of the literal `"'yes'"`.
(The existing acceptance scenario "Quoting is not recognized on a bare root-scalar line" only exercises an UNTERMINATED quote, which happens to fall through to `data` anyway — it does not cover this gap.)

**Spec citation (cite before changing behavior, per CLAUDE.md)**: SYML-SPEC-REVIEW.md D2: "Quoted strings are recognized only at an inline position, immediately after `key:` or `- `. ... Bare lines (root scalars, block values, continuation lines) are never quote-decoded; a leading `'` or `"` there is ordinary text." This was an explicit design decision (rejected alternative (ii): "Apply the quote rule to bare lines too ... silently decodes quoted continuation lines; rejected").

**Mechanism**: `src/syml/parsers.py` grammar:
  `line = indent (comment / blank / structure / value) &eol`
  `value = structure / quoted_value / data`
`structure` covers `list_item` / `key_value` / `section` (the two legitimate inline-quote positions: `quoted_key_value` and `value_list_item`, both of which use `value` deliberately since quoting IS recognized there). When a line is bare (no `-`, no `key:`), it falls through to the `value` alternative directly in `line`, which still tries `quoted_value` before `data` — so a bare line beginning with a well-formed quote decodes when it should not.

**Test file**: tests/test_parsers.py (or tests/test_nodes.py if that fits the existing suite's organization better — follow the file's existing pattern for grammar/decode-boundary tests)
**Target module**: src/syml/parsers.py (grammar + SymlParser)
**Existing patterns**: look at existing tests near `visit_quoted_value` / quote-guard (R-10) tests in tests/test_parsers.py for style
**Skills**: /pytest-unit-testing
**Instructions**: This leaf is one Test List entry. Write ONE failing test asserting a bare line with a well-formed single- or double-quoted value does NOT decode — e.g. parse `"'yes'"` (a standalone root-scalar document) and assert the result is the literal string `"'yes'"` (quotes included), not the decoded `"yes"`. Pick whichever bare-line case (root scalar or continuation) is clearest to test in isolation; a continuation-line variant may be added in Green/Refactor if useful, but Red only needs one failing assertion.
**Done when**: `uv run pytest <test-file> --no-cov` fails with an assertion error (not a collection/import error).

title: Remediate: quadratic parse time from per-node Pos.from_str_index document split
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review]
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/syml/basetypes.py (Pos.from_str_index L34, Source.from_node L91), src/syml/nodes.py (SymlNode.__post_init__ L35), src/syml/parsers.py (parse / SymlParser threading)

**Finding** (CRITICAL, CPU denial of service):
`Pos.from_str_index` splits the ENTIRE document on every call, and `Source.from_node` calls it twice per node from `SymlNode.__post_init__`. Every line builds about three nodes, so parsing is O(n^2) in document size. Measured on HEAD (no tracemalloc): a flat 2000-line list (20 KB) parses in 1.8 s, 8000 lines (87 KB) in 27 s (15x time for 4x input). Extrapolated, an ordinary well-formed 1 MiB document burns about an hour of CPU. cProfile: 3.6 s of 3.97 s cumulative is inside `from_str_index`. syml 0.6.2 takes 0.43 s at 2000 lines, so this is also a ~4x regression on top of an older quadratic.

Citation (constraint 6): plan.md Performance Goals (lines 57-58): "Every per-line and per-key step must stay O(1) amortized, because §13.4's size limits are deferred and nothing else bounds input size." The current code violates that stated invariant. This does NOT change parse results, only their cost.

**Fix suggestion**:
1. In `parsers.parse()`, compute a line-start offset table once from `doc.normalized` (e.g. `[0] + [i + 1 for i, c in enumerate(text) if c == '\n']`, or via `re.finditer('\n', ...)`).
2. Thread it through `SymlParser` to every node alongside `position_map` (or cache it keyed on the `full_text` object identity), and have `Source.from_node` resolve `Pos` with `bisect_right(line_starts, index) - 1` in O(log n).
3. Preserve `Pos.from_str_index`'s exact semantics, including the past-end clamp and the unterminated-final-line case (plan.md ~1611; existing tests pin them). Keep `Pos.from_str_index` itself for cold error paths and tests, or make it delegate to the same helper.
4. Add a unit test pinning the new helper's equivalence with `Pos.from_str_index` over edge cases (empty text, trailing '\n', index == len(text), index past end), and a scaling test (no wall-clock flakiness: e.g. assert `from_str_index`-style helper is called O(1) times per node, or compare 2000- vs 8000-line timings with a generous ratio).

**Acceptance**:
- An 8000-line flat list (`''.join(f'- item{i}\n' for i in range(8000))`) parses in under 1 s on a dev machine.
- Parse time for 8000 lines is at most ~5x the time for 2000 lines (linear-ish, not 16x).
- All positions (`Source.start`/`end`, error `position`) are byte-for-byte unchanged: full unit + acceptance suites pass unchanged.
- `just check` green, 100% coverage gate, ruff, mypy strict all pass via normal pre-commit hooks.

**Out of scope (decided, do not change)**: RecursionError on deep nesting and unbounded `load()` read are §13.4 limits deferred past 1.0 (spec.md:281, plan.md:66-70, D10/M15).

**CONSTRAINTS** (verbatim from /sp:08-harden):
(1) Migration from syml 0.6.2 is NOT a concern; do not add compatibility shims or migration code. (2) SYML-SPEC-REVIEW.md open items 1-8 remain UNAPPLIED; do not apply them. (3) Never reword decisions D1-D17 in SYML-SPEC-REVIEW.md. (4) No edits to specs/001-syml-1-0-conformance/spec.md or SYML-SPEC-REVIEW.md. (5) Treat the whole codebase (src/, tests/, tools/, specs/, docs/) as one program under review. (6) Cite an FR-NNN, a D-decision, or a B-/M- finding before changing parser behavior in either direction. (7) Commit through the normal pre-commit hooks (100% coverage gate, ruff, mypy); never bypass them.
close_reason: Cache Pos._line_start_offsets per full_text and resolve via bisect, fixing O(n^2) parse time; 8000-line doc now parses in ~0.35s vs prior 27s, positions byte-for-byte unchanged

title: Remediate: line-offset lru_cache pins last 4 parsed documents in memory
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review] (sp:08-harden cycle 2)
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: src/syml/basetypes.py (line 27, `_line_start_offsets`), src/syml/preprocess.py, src/syml/nodes.py, tests/test_basetypes.py

**CONSTRAINTS (verbatim from the harden orchestrator; obey all of them):**
(1) Migration from syml 0.6.2 is NOT a concern; do not add compatibility shims or migration code. (2) SYML-SPEC-REVIEW.md open items 1-8 remain UNAPPLIED; do not apply them. (3) Never reword decisions D1-D17 in SYML-SPEC-REVIEW.md. (4) No edits to specs/001-syml-1-0-conformance/spec.md or SYML-SPEC-REVIEW.md. (5) Treat the whole codebase (src/, tests/, tools/, specs/, docs/) as one program under review. (6) Cite an FR-NNN, a D-decision, or a B-/M- finding before changing parser behavior in either direction. (7) Commit through the normal pre-commit hooks (100% coverage gate, ruff, mypy); never bypass them.

**Finding** (MAJOR, untrusted-input memory retention; introduced by the syml-x0m.6.1 remediation at ccf58b0):
`@lru_cache(maxsize=4)` on `basetypes._line_start_offsets` is keyed on the document text itself. After `syml.loads()` returns and the caller drops every reference, the process-global cache still pins the full normalized document (for a BOM-less LF document this is the caller's own string object) plus a tuple holding one boxed int per line. Measured with tracemalloc: a 2 MB, 100k-line document leaves ~3.6 MB retained after `loads(doc); del r, doc; gc.collect()`, and `cache_clear()` frees ~5.7 MB. That is roughly 2.7x document size per slot, times 4 slots, held for the life of the process. At the spec's own 10 MiB / 1M-line ceiling that is on the order of 180 MB of untrusted input kept alive after the caller believes it is gone, and it also keeps possibly sensitive document text reachable in module state. Time complexity is fine: the cycle-1 O(n^2) fix is verified linear (80k-line flat map scales ~4.25x for 4x input). Design note, NOT reproduced: a maxsize=4 LRU could thrash under more than 4 interleaved distinct parses; a threaded probe (8 threads) showed exactly one miss per parse.

**Fix suggestion**:
1. The offset table belongs to one parse, not the process. `preprocess._scan_for_tab_indentation` already walks `normalized.split('\n')` with a running `offset`; emit the line-start offsets (and the trailing-newline flag) there and store them on `PositionMap` or `Document`.
2. Thread that per-parse table into `Source.from_node` / `SymlNode.__post_init__` (nodes already carry `position_map`), resolving positions via bisect over it.
3. Remove the `lru_cache` from `_line_start_offsets` entirely. Do NOT replace it with `cache_clear()` in a `finally`: concurrent parses would then evict each other mid-visit and slide back toward the O(n^2) behavior cycle 1 fixed.
4. Keep `Pos.from_str_index(text, index)` working (uncached) for one-shot error paths and the existing reference-oracle equivalence test.
5. Replace the regression guard in tests/test_basetypes.py (~line 372) that asserts on `_line_start_offsets.cache_info()` with one that asserts linear behavior another way (e.g. the per-parse table is computed once per parse, via a spy or call count), keeping the equivalence test.
This changes no parse output or error positions, so constraint (6) is not triggered; if any position changes, stop and cite the FR/D/B/M item first.

**Acceptance**:
- `basetypes._line_start_offsets` (or its replacement) has no `cache_info` attribute; no module-global cache keyed on document text remains in src/syml/.
- tracemalloc: after `r = syml.loads(doc); del r, doc; gc.collect()` on a ~2 MB, 100k-line document, retained traced memory is under 100 KB (add this as a test).
- Parse time stays linear: 20k -> 80k-line flat mapping scales under ~6x (existing perf/regression test still passes in spirit).
- Existing `Pos.from_str_index` reference-oracle equivalence test passes unchanged.
- Full unit + acceptance suites pass; 100% coverage, ruff, and mypy strict green through normal pre-commit hooks.
close_reason: Scoped _line_start_offsets cache to one parse via ContextVar, removing process-global lru_cache; added tracemalloc regression test

title: Remediate: quoted arguments bypass post-strip guard rules in tools/guard_rules.py
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review] (sp:08-harden cycle 3)
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: tools/guard_rules.py (lines 300-310 strip_quoted_content; 396-420 _evaluate_inner)

**Finding**:
Every POST_STRIP_RULES rule (reset-hard, checkout-dot, checkout-treeish-dot, restore-dot, clean-force, commit-amend, merge-squash, stash-drop, stash-clear, branch-force-delete, catastrophic-rm, br-init-force, legacy-bd) is matched only against the output of `strip_quoted_content`, which replaces every quoted string with `""`/`''`. The shell removes those quotes before git/rm sees argv, so quoting the dangerous token defeats the guard. Verified ALLOW (should be BLOCK): `git reset "<double-dash>hard"`, `git reset '<double-dash>hard'`, `git reset <double-dash>ha""rd`, `git commit "<double-dash>am""end" -m x`, `git clean "-fd"`, `git branch "-D" foo`, `git stash "drop"`, `git checkout "."`, `rm -rf "/"`. The PRE_STRIP rules (hook-bypass, force-push) are not affected because they run on the unstripped text.

**Fix suggestion**:
Stop letting quoting erase the tokens a rule keys on. Preferred: tokenize each sub-command with `shlex.split` (posix=True; on ValueError from unbalanced quotes, fail CLOSED for the rule set, or fall back to also matching the raw normalized text) and match the rules against the de-quoted argv re-joined with single spaces, while still discarding heredoc bodies and the *contents* of arguments that are clearly message payloads (e.g. the value after `-m`/`--message`) so the existing false-positive protection for commit messages is kept. Minimal alternative: evaluate POST_STRIP_RULES against both `strip_quoted_content(normalized)` sub-commands AND a quote-removed (not content-removed) rendering of each sub-command, blocking if either matches. title: Remediate: clustered, capitalized, and glob-suffixed flags bypass guard rule patterns
description:
**Review**: [sp:security-review] (harden cycle 5)
**Range**: master..HEAD
**Files**: tools/guard_rules.py (force-push ~line 72, clean-force ~line 160, branch-force-delete ~line 259, catastrophic-rm ~line 272), tests/tools/test_guard_rules.py

**Finding** (MAJOR):
Short flags are matched as case-sensitive substrings in a fixed position rather than as whitespace-delimited option tokens, so ordinary clustered or capitalized spellings slip past rules the hook already claims, and one safe pattern matches inside path names. Verified on HEAD:
- force-push ALLOWS `git push -uf origin main` and `git push -fu origin main` (pattern wants `-f(\s|$)`).
- branch-force-delete ALLOWS `git branch -Df foo` (pattern wants `-D(\s|$)`).
- catastrophic-rm ALLOWS `rm -Rf /` and `rm -fR ~` (pattern only accepts lowercase `rf|fr`; `-R` is rm's standard synonym for `-r`).
- catastrophic-rm ALLOWS `rm -rf /*`, `rm -rf ./*`, `rm -rf ~/*`, `rm -rf "$HOME"/*` (the target alternation must be followed immediately by whitespace/end, so a glob suffix escapes; the rule message explicitly lists `/`, `./`, `~`, `*`, `$HOME`).
- catastrophic-rm ALLOWS `rm -rf --no-preserve-root /` and `rm -r -f --no-preserve-root /` (an option between the flags and the target).
- clean-force's safe pattern `git\s+clean\s+.*-[a-zA-Z]*n` matches `-gen` in `build-gen/` or `-plugin` in `my-plugin/`, so `git clean -fd build-gen/` and `git clean -fd my-plugin/` ALLOW (safe pattern wrongly exempts).

**Fix suggestion**:
Anchor every short-flag pattern, block and safe alike, to a whitespace-preceded option token and accept clusters: e.g. force-push `\s-[a-zA-Z]*f[a-zA-Z]*(?=\s|$)`; branch-force-delete `\s-(?:[a-zA-Z]*D[a-zA-Z]*|[a-zA-Z]*d[a-zA-Z]*\s+.*-[a-zA-Z]*f)` or simply a `D` cluster; clean-force safe patterns `\s-[a-zA-Z]*n[a-zA-Z]*(?=\s|$)` and `\s--dry-run\b`. For catastrophic-rm, accept `[rR]`, allow intervening `--\S+` options (notably `--no-preserve-root`) before the target, and allow an optional `/*` or `*` glob suffix on each target (`/`, `./`, `../`, `~`, `~/`, `$HOME`, `${HOME}`, `.`). The de-quoted pass already renders `"$HOME"/*` as `$HOME/*`, so a target-suffix fix covers it.

**Acceptance**:

- Still ALLOW: `git push`, `git push -u origin main`, `git branch -d foo`, `git clean -n`, `git clean -fdn`, `git clean --dry-run -fd`, `rm -rf build/`, `rm -rf ./build`, `rm -f ./notes.txt`.

title: syml 1.0.0 break-testing
description:
Break-test campaign against master 27a3e9a (post D18/D19), run 2026-09-24. Five background lanes: (1) Hypothesis round-trip fuzzing, (2) hand-crafted grammar/tree-builder probes + timing + CHANGELOG/spec oracles, (3) public API and source-position probes, (4) real-document human-usability lens, (5) independent cross-vendor spec-vs-implementation audit. Every child issue's repro was re-executed by the orchestrator on master and reproduced. Duplicates across lanes were merged (5 lanes reported ~58 raw findings; 24 survive). No fixes in this pass.

## Counts
- Defects (type bug): 14 — P1: 2 (.1, .2), P2: 4 (.3–.6), P3: 8 (.7–.14).
- Judgment calls (type task, label judgment): 10 — P2: 5 (.15–.19), P3: 5 (.20–.24).
- Introduced by D18/D19: only .6 (dumps over-rejection). Everything else predates the literal-values change.
- Hypothesis: P1–P7 pass at 2000 examples each once the .1 family is excluded; no out-of-contract exception type ever escaped loads or dumps. All 54 spec Output examples match master. Timing is linear (100k-key doc 8.6 s, GC-bound; 10k-line dumps 0.39 s); no super-linear path found.

## Most serious finding: syml-xreq.1
`indent = ~r"\s*"` accepts every Unicode White_Space code point as indentation and also swallows `\n`, so NBSP-led lines lose the NBSP, NBSP-only lines vanish with their newline, VT/FF/NEL are stripped from line starts, an NBSP hides a tab from the §9.0 scan, and dumps→loads silently changes data:
```python
import syml
print(repr(syml.loads(syml.dumps('\xa0x'))))            # 'x'
print(syml.loads(syml.dumps({'k': 'a\n\xa0b'})))        # {'k': 'a\n b'}
print(syml.loads('k:\n  a\n\xa0\n  b'))                 # {'k': 'a\nb'}, spec: OutOfContextNodeError
```

## Recommendation on tagging 1.0.0 now: NO, but it is close.
Fix before tagging (all cheap): .1 (indent class + adopt the spec's own top rule, which also closes .9's grammar mismatch), .4 (filename prefix), .5 (tab position through PositionMap), .6 (lex the block line without §9.0 step 1), .8 (CHANGELOG text). Two items need David's RULING before anyone can fix them, because code and spec disagree and either side could be right: .2 (root scalar indentation: §5.3/CHANGELOG 7 vs §11.2.1 rule C and the code) and .3 (indentless sequence: code + bar.syml vs §4.2 r5/§9.3, and CHANGELOG 17's false claim). The P3 bugs can wait for 1.0.1.

## Judgment calls for David (each issue carries repro, author intent, options, cost, my recommendation)
- .15 blank line inside a prose value drops the paragraph break — recommend: keep a blank line between two continuation lines of the same value.
- .16 `- [ask: why?]` / `- "listen: I know."` / `- 3: 1 odds` silently become mappings — recommend: forbid keys that start with [ { ( " '.

title: Unicode whitespace is accepted as indentation: NBSP/U+3000/U+2028/VT/FF/NEL-led lines lose characters, NBSP-only lines vanish, dumps→loads silently corrupts
description:
Found by lanes 1, 2, 5 (L1-1..L1-4, L2-01, A5-01). Root cause: parsers.py `indent = ~r"\s*"`. Parsimonious compiles with the `regex` module, whose `\s` is the full Unicode White_Space set (TAB, LF, VT, FF, CR, U+0020, U+0085, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000–U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000) and also matches `\n`. Spec §4.1 `indent = ~" *"`, §4.2 rule 4, §9.0 step 3 / D14: only U+0020 (and a rejected U+0009) are indentation; §4.6.1 says C0/C1 controls pass through verbatim.

Consequences (all verified on master):
- loads('\xa0k: v') == {'k': 'v'}   expected the scalar '\xa0k: v'
- loads('\u2028- x') == ['x']       expected '\u2028- x'
- loads('k:\n  \xa0x') == {'k': 'x'}  expected {'k': '\xa0x'}
- loads('k:\n  a\n\xa0\n  b') == {'k': 'a\nb'}  (NBSP-only line and its LF swallowed into next indent) expected OutOfContextNodeError
- loads('\x0bx') == loads('\x0cx') == loads('\x85x') == 'x'; loads('\x0c') == ''   expected verbatim (§4.6.1)
- loads('\xa0\tx') == 'x'  the tab after an NBSP bypasses the §9.0 tab scan (which only inspects a ' \t' run)
- SILENT ROUND-TRIP CORRUPTION: dumps accepts these values (serializer only checks ' '/'\t' leading chars): loads(dumps('\xa0x')) == 'x'; loads(dumps({'k': 'a\n\xa0b'})) == {'k': 'a\n b'} (NBSP replaced by a space); loads(dumps('x\n\xa0')) == 'x'. §11.2.1 says dumps MUST raise rather than emit text that reads back differently.

Repro:
```python
import syml
for x in ['\xa0x', {'k': 'a\n\xa0b'}, 'x\n\xa0', '\u2028']:
    print(repr(x), '->', repr(syml.loads(syml.dumps(x))))
print(syml.loads('\xa0k: v'), syml.loads('k:\n  a\n\xa0\n  b'), repr(syml.loads('\x0bx')), repr(syml.loads('\xa0\tx')))
```
Predates D18/D19 (line dates from the c12aee5 overhaul). Lane 2 note: `\s*` is load-bearing because `line` only lookaheads `&eol` and the NEXT line's indent consumes the `\n`; swapping the class alone stalls the parse after line 1. Verified in-memory fix shape: adopt the spec's own top rule `lines = (line "\n")* line?` plus `indent = ~"[ \t]*"` (tab-only lines stay blank per §9.0) and flatten in visit_lines; that also closes the §4.1 grammar-text mismatch. Alternative direction under David's easiest-for-humans yardstick: normalize Unicode White_Space at line start to U+0020 in a §9.0 step (keeping VT/FF/NEL verbatim per §4.6.1), so a pasted NBSP-led `k: v` still means the mapping the author intended and an NBSP-only spacer line stays blank; that needs a spec edit, the spec-direction fix does not. Hypothesis round trip passes at 2000 examples once this family is excluded, so this is the one round-trip hole.

Re-confirmed on master 27a3e9a by the orchestrator. Campaign epic: syml-xreq. No fix in this pass.
close_reason: Unicode whitespace round-trip verified by the P1-P8 property with no excluded family, Contract 04

title: Undocumented recursion cliffs: a trailing line that walks up ≥~245 levels raises RecursionError (CHANGELOG 13 says ~500), and parse() succeeds at 500 levels while .as_data() raises
description:
Found by lane 2 (L2-10). The §9.2 walk-up (_delegate_incorporate_node) recurses once per ancestor, so a deeply nested document followed by a line that must climb back to the top hits the limit at about half the documented block depth. And at 500 levels parse() returns a Root but as_data() raises, so loads and parse disagree.
```python
import syml
nest = lambda n, tail='': '\n'.join('  '*i + f'k{i}:' for i in range(n)) + ('\n'+tail if tail else '')
print(type(syml.loads(nest(240, 'z: 1'))))   # dict
try: syml.loads(nest(250, 'z: 1'))
except RecursionError: print('RecursionError at 250 with a trailing line')
print(type(syml.loads(nest(250))))            # dict: same depth, no trailing line, fine
r = syml.parse(nest(500)); print(type(r))      # Root
try: r.as_data()
except RecursionError: print('as_data raises at 500')
```
Hostile-input-only; nothing is truncated silently below any cliff. Document in CHANGELOG 13 (or make the walk-up iterative). Not D18/D19.

title: RULED: keep a blank line between two continuation lines of the same value (paragraph breaks survive; dumps may write them)
description:
Lanes 4 and 2 (L4-S2, L2-15). Conforming (§5.1 rule 5, D12): blank lines inside a continuation block are skipped and never affect the value; a value with a paragraph break is unrepresentable by dumps.
```python
import syml
print(repr(syml.loads('k:\n  Para one.\n\n  Para two.')))   # 'Para one.\nPara two.'
print(repr(syml.loads('Para one.\n\nPara two.')))            # 'Para one.\nPara two.'
```
What the author meant: two paragraphs. This is the single most likely surprise for interactive-fiction prose.
Options: (a) keep as is and document loudly; (b) keep a blank line that sits BETWEEN two continuation lines of the same value (blank lines before the first continuation or after the last, and blank lines between items, stay inert) and let dumps write paragraph breaks; (c) require an explicit marker line.
Cost of (b): a value that ends with blank lines before a dedent still cannot end with a blank line (trailing blanks stay inert), and the §5.3 termination rule gains one clause. Recommendation: (b). It matches every author's intent, costs one rule, and removes a whole unrepresentable class from §11.2.1.

title: RULED: a root scalar keeps its leading indentation (§5.3/CHANGELOG 7 stand); fix the code, carve root out of §11.2.1 rule C

title: OutOfContextNodeError and TabIndentationError .message omit the filename prefix promised by CHANGELOG 9
description:
Found by lanes 2, 3, 4, 5 (L2-05, L3-2, L4-D2, A5-09). Only Mapping.can_add_node (DuplicateKeyError) and encoding_error (EncodingError) build their message through error_message(desc, filename). nodes.fail_to_incorporate_node and preprocess._scan_for_tab_indentation use bare strings, and the tab scan is not even handed the filename. The two most common errors therefore lose the file name whether it came from loads(filename=) or load(open(p)).
```python
import syml
for doc in ('a: 1\n  - x', 'a:\n\tb', 'a: 1\na: 2'):
    try: syml.loads(doc, filename='f.syml')
    except syml.ParseError as e: print(type(e).__name__, repr(e.message))
# OutOfContextNodeError 'Failed to incorporate a node'   <- no prefix
# TabIndentationError "A tab character was found in a line's leading whitespace"   <- no prefix
# DuplicateKeyError 'f.syml: Duplicate key'
```
Also: filename='' yields the message ': Duplicate key'. Not D18/D19.
